newsitem.title: UK: Boots shares drop after Q1 sales update.
newsitem.headline: Boots shares drop after Q1 sales update.

text.p: Shares in retailer Boots Co Plc Co Plc fell in early trade on Thursday, after a disappointing trading statement prompted profit-taking in the stock, dealers said.
Boots shares, which reached a record 842p on July 22, were down 24p at 792 by 0743 GMT in trade of 804,596 shares.
"The figures were a little disappointing, the stock has had a run and there will be analysts downgrading after this statement," said one senior dealer.

In a statement due to be released at its annual meeting, Boots said group sales for the first quarter rose almost 11 percent from last year with like-for-like sales at Boots the Chemist, its largest chain, up 5.1 percent.

"Looking ahead, market conditions continue to be satisfactory for our businesses," said chief executive James Blyth. "We believe that we have strategies and people in place to continue the delivery of long-term growth."

Yet analysts said the performance of Boots' Do-It-All unit, where like-for-like sales rose by just 2.4 percent, looked disappointing, undermining the stock's market valuation, which had lately approached that of Marks & Spencer Plc.

"The case for Boots has been based on the phenomenal growth of Boots the Chemists, but what we want to know is its ability to generate any growth elsewhere," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
Mark Charnock, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney, said the results from the core chemists chain looked sound but other parts of the group were less promising.

"If Boots the Chemists is doing OK it should be good news for the company as a whole," Charnock said. "But the shares had risen a hell of a long way and sometimes people just wait for an event like this to crystallise some profits."
By 0823 GMT the stock was down 29p at 787 in volume of 2.1 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the London market at that point.
